data.title: STOCKS | Australian Equities Record Biggest Weekly Rout Since 2022 as Miners Slump
data.description: Australian equities suffered their biggest weekly rout in more than four years as mining stocks slumped, Bloomberg reported. The decline tracked a deepening global selloff driven by strains in the artificial intelligence trade.

data.title: Attacker Suspected of Stealing 5.2 Million XMR1 Sells Tokens and Buys 7,467 ETH
data.description: An attacker suspected of stealing 5.2 million XMR1 sold the tokens on Hyperliquid and used the proceeds to buy Ether. According to Foresight News, Lookonchain tracked the activity and reported that the attacker had spent 13.22 million USDC to purchase 7,467 ETH as of the latest update.

data.title: Binance to Add Six Tokens to Monitoring Tag and Remove Seed Tags From MORPHO, HYPE
data.description: According to the announcement from Binance, the exchange will add Lorenzo Protocol (BANK), Initia (INIT), Mitosis (MITO), Harmony (ONE), THENA (THE) and Zilliqa (ZIL) to its Monitoring Tag list on 2026-11-20. Binance will also remove the Seed Tag from Morpho Token (MORPHO) and Hyperliquid (HYPE). The exchange said the changes follow recent reviews and that tags for the tokens will be updated shortly after the announcement is published. Binance said tokens carrying a Monitoring Tag are subject to notably higher volatility and risks than other listed tokens. The exchange reviews these tokens periodically and may determine that they no longer meet its listing criteria, which could result in delisting. Reviews consider factors including a project team’s commitment, development activity, trading volume and liquidity, network and smart contract stability, public communication, responsiveness to due diligence requests, token supply or tokenomics changes, evidence of unethical or fraudulent conduct, and contributions to the crypto ecosystem. Binance stated that other services related to the named tokens will not be affected by the tag changes.

data.title: PowerCompute’s 267 Bitcoin Collateral Sale Repays Nearly $22 Million Loan, Secured Debt Falls to $1.25 Million
data.description: About 267 Bitcoin pledged by Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin miner PowerCompute were sold by lender Arch Lending on September 24, with the proceeds used to repay nearly $22 million in loan principal and reduce secured debt to $1.25 million. According to Odaily, Arch Lending co-founder Himanshu Sahay said PowerCompute directed the sale as part of a corporate strategic adjustment, not in response to a market event. PowerCompute’s 10-Q filing submitted last week showed the company had about $650,000 in cash at the end of September, and substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern remained unresolved. The company plans to raise funds through debt refinancing and a stock offering, which has about $71 million in remaining capacity.

data.title: DayOne Puts Multibillion-Dollar US IPO on Hold as Investors Question Data Center Valuations
data.description: According to Bloomberg, DayOne Data Centers Ltd. has put its multibillion-dollar US initial public offering on hold, people familiar with the matter said. Investors have questioned whether valuations for digital infrastructure supporting the artificial intelligence boom are sustainable.

data.title: CME XRP Futures Reach $81.2 Billion in Notional Volume 18 Months After Launch
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin.com, CME Group announced on November 19 that its standard and micro XRP futures had recorded $81.2 billion in notional volume in the 18 months since launch. Through November 16, 2026, the contracts had traded 1.9 million contracts, with average daily notional volume of $216 million and volume equivalent to 42.8 billion XRP.

CME said, citing CoinGlass data, that its XRP futures accounted for about 18.5% of open interest across tracked exchanges at 1:03 AM (UTC+8) on November 20, 2026, ranking first.

data.title: SK Hynix Reportedly Considers Converting Kioxia-Related Bonds Into Shares
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, industry sources said Friday that SK Hynix is considering converting convertible bonds it holds in connection with its investment in Kioxia, a Japanese NAND flash memory maker, into shares. Sources said the move is apparently intended to strengthen SK Hynix’s position as Kioxia’s largest shareholder.

In 2018, SK Hynix invested in Kioxia through a consortium led by Bain Capital and comprising investors from South Korea, the United States and Japan. The investment included convertible bonds and an equity fund, totaling 395 billion yen, or about 3.8 trillion won. In June this year, as part of a shareholder-return plan, SK Hynix sold its entire stake in the fund, into which it had initially invested 2.6 trillion won. The company had said it would distribute capital gains from the sale to shareholders through a special dividend starting in the third quarter of this year.

Sources familiar with the matter said SK Hynix does not plan to sell its remaining investment immediately after converting the bonds into shares, so the conversion would not immediately change its stake in Kioxia. They added that SK Hynix intends to maintain cooperation with the Japanese chipmaker while respecting Kioxia’s independent management.

data.title: APEC Releases Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework for 2027–2030
data.description:
According to Jin10, the APEC Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027–2030) was released. It encourages APEC economies to ensure electronic signatures have legal effect and are not denied that effect solely because they are in electronic form, and to cooperate voluntarily to promote their use and mutual recognition.

The framework also encourages economies to improve their legal frameworks for domestic electronic transactions by referring to principles in the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce (1996), the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures (2001), the United Nations Convention on the Use of Electronic Communications in International Contracts (2005), or the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (2017), while accounting for differences in economies’ development and capabilities.

APEC economies support a temporary exemption from customs duties on electronic transmissions, which helps maintain an open and predictable digital market. The framework notes efforts by some economies to reach an agreement for a permanent exemption from customs duties on electronic transmissions, and recognizes the importance of including such exemptions in trade agreements.

data.title: Oil Prices Fall, but Bond Yields Stay High as Inflation Concerns Persist
data.description:
According to Jin10, the Financial Times reported that global bond markets had shown a strong correlation between oil prices and government borrowing costs this year, but the relationship has now broken down. Despite a decline in global crude benchmarks in recent weeks, bond yields and expectations for interest rate hikes remain elevated. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remains above 5%, not far below the high reached last month, its highest level since 2002.

Some investors warned that inflation pressures are becoming entrenched after a series of supply shocks. Resilient U.S. economic growth has also fueled bets on hawkish measures. Ales Koutny, head of international rates at Vanguard Group, said government bonds had become “decoupled” from oil prices and had returned to their original characteristics. John Stopford, head of multi-asset income at Ninety One, said weak bond performance was “a reaction to hawkish central bank rhetoric, reflecting the market’s frustration with persistently stubborn inflation.” Greg Peters, co-chief investment officer for fixed income at PGIM, said inflation was like a virus that is difficult to remove once it enters the economic system.

data.title: Bloomberg Economist: Anthropic's Massive IPO May Be the AI Rally's Last Fuel
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bloomberg Economics, economist Anna Wong said Anthropic's large IPO may be the AI rally's “last fuel,” rather than the start of another upswing. Since September, the cutoff for financial data in Anthropic's prospectus, its realized price per million tokens has fallen sharply. Token usage has surged, but its market share has not increased and may have edged down, Wong said, suggesting the company has surrendered some pricing premium without strengthening its competitive position.

Large fundraising could support the AI trade in the short term. After listing, however, public markets will scrutinize frontier AI pricing, margins and returns on capital each quarter. If Anthropic's results show weaker pricing power than its valuation implies, a repricing could accelerate valuation declines across the AI sector, Wong said.

data.title: Japan's 10-Year Government Bond Yield Falls 3.0 Basis Points to 2.790%
data.description: According to Jin10, Japan's 10-year government bond yield fell 3.0 basis points to 2.790%.

data.title: Hyperbeat Launches USD+ Stablecoin for Risk-Adjusted Yield Across Hyperliquid
data.description:
Hyperbeat, a native yield layer in the Hyperliquid ecosystem, has launched USD+, a stablecoin product that offers risk-adjusted yield across the ecosystem. According to Foresight News, USD+ allocates funds across Morpho markets, HyperLend, Hyperliquid Earn USDC, Liquid Bank credit markets, and delta-neutral strategies.

Users can use USD+ as collateral in Liquid Banking to borrow up to 85% of its value while continuing to earn yield, with borrowed funds available for trading, spending, or withdrawal. Hyperbeat also introduced Builder Codes to support native integration of USD+ into front ends.

data.title: Ethereum Spot ETFs See $131M Net Outflow, Led by BlackRock’s ETHA
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing RootData, U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $131 million in net outflows yesterday, November 19 (U.S. Eastern Time). BlackRock’s ETHA led with $124 million in outflows, followed by Grayscale’s ETHE with $5.2 million.

data.title: Bubblemaps Says Crypto KOL Daumen Made About $340,000 Using Linked Wallets Around Token Calls
data.description:
Bubblemaps said crypto KOL Daumen traded more than 5,000 tokens alongside his public wallet through nine linked wallets since April, with linked-wallet activity involving 760 tokens. According to Foresight News, the wallets often bought in the same block, after which Daumen posted calls that pushed prices up; the linked wallets sold first, followed by his public wallet.

The linked wallets reportedly made about $340,000 across those 760 tokens, while the public wallet earned about $50,000. Bubblemaps also said the public wallet funded a deployment address associated with a developer who has launched more than 400 tokens since October and quickly sold them.

data.title: Moody’s Downgrades Nvidia’s Credit Outlook From Positive to Stable
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Chang'an Jie Zhi Shi, Moody’s Ratings lowered Nvidia’s credit outlook from positive to stable, citing governance concerns following the departure of longtime CEO Jensen Huang; the Global Times reported the move on November 19, citing Bloomberg. Moody’s said an upgrade was unlikely within the next 12 to 18 months, and its analysts said Huang’s departure had added uncertainty to Nvidia’s business strategy and financial policies. The agency’s outlook categories are positive, stable, negative and developing.

Nvidia announced on November 12 that its board had approved Huang’s resignation as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. On November 17, Huang said in his first public statement since stepping down that he would be willing to return as CEO if invited by the board. The board chair said on November 18 that the company did not plan to reinstate him and would consider internal and external candidates. Interim CEO Colette Kress told a companywide meeting on Wednesday, “Let’s look forward.”

The report said executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, tasked by Nvidia’s board with finding a new president, had contacted Arm CEO Rene Haas about the position. Other candidates reportedly include Nvidia Vice President Ian Buck, AMD CEO Lisa Su and Apple Chief Hardware Officer Johny Srouji.

On November 20 (UTC+8), Nvidia shares fell to an intraday low of $145.74 and closed at $145.98, giving the company a market capitalization of $3.52 trillion. The stock fell for a sixth straight session, erasing about $668.8 billion in market value, equivalent to approximately RMB 4.46197 trillion. Since the events involving Huang began, Nvidia shares have fallen nearly 31.7%, erasing about $1.63 trillion in market value, or approximately RMB 10.95 trillion.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | USCC Says Beijing Seeks Industry Advantage Amid US-China Trade Tensions
data.description: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission’s annual report examines economic, technology and national security challenges posed by China. Chair Randy Schriver and Vice-Chair Mike Kuiken said Beijing continues to seek an advantage over the US in many industries globally despite increased dialogue between the countries’ leaders, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Japan's Top Property Insurers Report Cyber Claim Surge
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Japan's largest property insurers are reporting a sharp rise in cyber insurance claims as AI-driven attacks grow more sophisticated and hacking incidents surge nationwide.
